anning and Development Services Committee Meeting - November 30, 2026
Public Meeting
Land Acknowledgement
The City of Oshawa is situated on lands within the traditional and treaty territory of the Michi Saagiig and Chippewa Anishinaabeg and the signatories of the Williams Treaties, which include the Mississaugas of Scugog Island, Curve Lake, Hiawatha and Alderville First Nations, and the Chippewas of Georgina Island, Rama and Beausoleil First Nations.
We are grateful for the Anishinaabeg who have cared for the land and waters within this territory since time immemorial.
We recognize that Oshawa is steeped in rich Indigenous history and is now present day home to many First Nations, Inuit and Métis people. We express gratitude for this diverse group of Indigenous Peoples who continue to care for the land and shape and strengthen our community.
As a municipality, we are committed to understanding the truth of our shared history, acknowledging our role in addressing the negative impacts that colonization continues to have on Indigenous Peoples, developing reciprocal relationships, and taking meaningful action toward reconciliation.
We are all Treaty people.

PDSC-26-04 Development Charge By-law Amendment for Temporary Sales Offices (All Wards)
1.
PDSC-26-04.pdf
Recommendation
That the Planning and Development Services Committee recommend to Council:
Whereas the City of Oshawa Development Charges By-law 91-2024, as amended, provides an exemption from City development charges for a temporary building or structure and defines “Temporary” as a use for a period not exceeding three (3) years; and,
Whereas temporary sales offices are often needed for periods of time longer than three (3) years depending on site and market conditions; and,
Whereas currently, after three (3) years, the sales office would be required to be demolished, moved or incur commercial development charges; and,
Whereas temporary sales offices are often temporarily placed over future residential lots that once developed, will be subject to development charges; and,
Whereas the City of Oshawa Zoning By-law 60-94, as amended, permits a temporary sales office associated with an approved plan of subdivision or condominium to remain until all lots or dwelling units have been sold; and,
Whereas it is appropriate to align the development charge exemption applicable to temporary sales offices with the period during which such a sales office is permitted to remain under the Zoning By-law;
Therefore be it resolved that City of Oshawa Development Charges By-law 91-2024, as amended, be further amended to provide that, notwithstanding the definition of “Temporary” in Section 1.1, for the purposes of Section 3.6(j), a temporary sales office permitted in accordance with Section 4.13 of Zoning By-law 60-94, as amended, or any successor thereto, shall be considered a Temporary building or structure for so long as the temporary sales office is permitted to remain under the applicable provisions of the Zoning By-law.
